prompt:
The GAL-TAN framework identifies political orientation on a single axis. Individuals and texts are placed according to the degree to which their views align with either pole, as follows:

  - Individuals at the GAL (Green/Alternative/Libertarian) pole support expanded
    personal freedoms and social liberalisation, for example: access to abortion,
    same-sex marriage, environmental protection, and multiculturalism.

  - Individuals at the TAN (Traditional/Authoritarian/Nationalist) pole prioritise
    order, tradition, and stability, and believe that the state should treat the
    maintenance of national identity as a priority, for example: restrictive
    immigration policy, emphasis on law and order, defence of traditional social
    institutions, and national sovereignty over supranational authority.

A text occupies a position on this axis to the extent that it argues FROM these commitments, not to the extent that it mentions the associated topics:

  - Environmental or immigration policy discussed in administrative or fiscal
    terms does not by itself indicate a position.
  - Nuclear expansion argued for energy security is not GAL.
  - Faster asylum processing argued on humanitarian grounds is not TAN.

The profile below describes the positional priorities of the British electorate.

<profile>
  tan: 0.76
  gal: 0.24
</profile>

Below are two texts.

TEXT_D:
The Liberal Democrats’ Real Alternative is a costed, green, liberal programme built on Freedom, Fairness and Trust, with power devolved from Westminster and a strong internationalist outlook. A “green thread” runs throughout.

Fair, simple, affordable government
- Fully costed plans, switching around £5bn a year from low-priority spend (abolish unnecessary subsidies and the DTI’s wasteful functions; scrap ID cards; redirect the Child Trust Fund) to frontline priorities.
- One net tax rise: a 50% rate only on income over £100,000 to fund abolishing tuition and top-up fees, free personal care for the elderly and disabled, and lower local taxes.
- Replace the unfair Council Tax with a Local Income Tax based on ability to pay, saving the typical household about £450 a year; raise the stamp duty threshold to £150,000.

Putting patients first
- Free personal care for older and disabled people; more doctors, nurses and therapists; sweep away pointless central targets so clinicians and locally accountable bodies decide.
- Faster diagnosis via the quickest practical route; expand scans/tests (evenings/weekends), publish diagnostic waits.
- Free eye and dental checks; extend prescription charge exemptions; rebuild NHS dentistry; legislate for better mental health rights; ban smoking in enclosed public places; hardwire prevention and clean environments into health.

Ambitious for every child and learner
- Abolish tuition/top-up fees; restore fair grants; equalise college/school funding; modernise skills with a 14–19 diploma blending vocational and academic routes.
- Cut infant class sizes to an average of 20 (junior to 25) by hiring 21,000 teachers; extend wraparound care and complete 3,500 Children’s Centres.
- Less high-stakes testing; strengthen discipline and SEND support.

Tackling crime, defending liberty
- 10,000 more police by cancelling ID cards; cut red tape so officers patrol, not paperwork.
- Smart justice: tough community penalties for non-violent offenders; focus on traffickers and acquisitive crime.
- Repeal control-order regime; defend jury trial; prosecute terror in open courts (including intercept evidence); create a UK Border Force.
- Fair asylum decisions by a dedicated agency; allow asylum seekers to work; Single Equality Act and hate-crime units; specialist Environmental Tribunal.

Prosperity with less red tape, more green growth
- Independent budget scrutiny by the NAO; simpler, fairer business taxes; small-business rate relief; “sunset clauses” on regulation; duty to trade fairly; boost tourism.
- Green fiscal reform: shift to a Carbon Tax; incentives for efficient homes/clean vehicles; at least 20% electricity from renewables by 2020; do not replace ageing nuclear; promote hydrogen and clean tech.

Security, rights and global leadership
- Iraq was wrong; rebuild through the UN/EU, include Sunnis, strengthen Iraqi forces, and aim to withdraw UK troops with the UN mandate’s expiry.
- Support EU reform and the Constitution via referendum; prepare to join the euro when conditions are right; managed economic migration.
- Right-size procurement (cut Eurofighter Tranche 3) to fund troops’ welfare; retain a minimum nuclear deterrent while driving multilateral disarmament; tighten arms export controls.

Fair pensions and support
- Citizen’s Pension from 75 with earnings link (ending means-testing for around a million); Local Income Tax benefits eight in ten pensioners; £170/week Maternity Income Guarantee for six months; scrap the CSA and move enforcement to HMRC; extend Winter Fuel Payment to severely disabled adults; robust anti-fraud simplification.

Stronger local communities, rural fairness, better transport
- Devolve power, cut inspectorates to a streamlined Audit Commission; protect post offices and universal mail.
- Release public land to build 100,000 affordable homes; favour brownfield; control second homes where markets are distorted.
- Fair farm/food trading (Food Trade Inspector); CAP reform for public goods; Marine Act; Animal Welfare Commission; strict GM safeguards, promote organic.
- Fix rail with fewer, longer franchises and key upgrades; reward cleaner cars; expand congestion charging with upfront transit investment; plan national road-user charging to replace fuel/vehicle taxes; limit new roads; greener aviation taxes; free off-peak buses for pensioners/disabled and free railcards for target groups.

Better government
- Curb Prime Ministerial power (War Powers Act; Civil Service Act); predominantly elected second chamber; STV for all elections and votes at 16; deeper devolution; independent BBC regulator; Environmental Responsibility Act and a unified Environment–Transport–Energy department.

Climate leadership
- Beat UK Kyoto targets early; lead toward “contraction and convergence”; scale renewables, efficiency and recycling; help households cut bills and carbon.

TEXT_F:
Are you thinking what we’re thinking? Britain is a great country heading in the wrong direction. After years of Labour talk, the forgotten majority who work hard, pay their taxes and do the right thing deserve action that rewards responsibility, restores discipline, devolves power, and secures our borders. Conservatives will focus on cleaner hospitals, school discipline, more police, controlled immigration and lower taxes—with clear accountability for delivery.

- Value for money and lower taxes: Save £12bn a year by 2007–08 by cutting waste, quangos and bureaucracy; use £8bn to reduce borrowing (avoiding stealth taxes) and £4bn for tax cuts. Match or exceed Labour on the NHS, schools, transport and aid; spend more on police, defence and pensions. Restore dignity in retirement by linking the basic state pension to earnings and halving council tax bills (up to £500) for many pensioners. Promote saving via Lifetime Savings Accounts and stronger company pensions. Cut red tape with regulatory budgets and sunset reviews; end EU gold-plating; restore the UK opt-out from the Social Chapter; keep Bank of England independence; no Euro.

- Family support, childcare and school discipline: More flexible maternity pay; up to £50/week per under‑5 for working families via tax credits, for formal or informal childcare. Restore order: heads control admissions and expulsions; Turnaround Schools for disruptors; protect teachers and cut paperwork. Money follows the pupil; expand good schools with 600,000 extra places; allow free places at independent schools at state cost; moratorium on closing special schools. Raise standards: tougher, more transparent exams and a slimmer, rigorous curriculum. Back skills and health: 300,000 vocational grants; two hours after‑school sport; ban junk food in schools. Scrap university tuition fees; abolish the admissions regulator; build university endowments.

- Better healthcare and cleaner hospitals: Increase NHS funding and drive it to the front line; abolish targets and Strategic Health Authorities; slim PCTs and quangos. Empower clinicians; bring back Matron with power to close wards for cleaning; invest in infection control and more single rooms. Funding follows the patient; protect community hospitals. Recognise self‑funders with a contribution worth half the NHS cost to cut waiting. End waiting lists this Parliament. Support carers; protect homes through a social‑care partnership; fix NHS dentistry. Health checks for non‑EU migrants; a bold STI public‑health campaign.

- Safer communities: 5,000 extra police each year; slash paperwork; elected police commissioners; zero‑tolerance neighbourhood policing. 20,000 extra prison places; end early release; honesty in sentencing. Expand rehab to 25,000 places; return cannabis to Class B. Robust counter‑terror laws and a Homeland Security Minister.

- Secure borders and controlled immigration: British Border Control Police; 24‑hour port surveillance. Australian‑style points system prioritising needed skills. Take back asylum control, withdraw from the 1951 Convention, process claims offshore, and set an annual, Parliament‑approved limit including a UNHCR refugee quota.

- Accountability and local power: Publish a Timetable for Action; sack failing ministers. Abolish regional assemblies; return powers on planning, housing, transport and fire to councils. Strengthen Parliament; cut MPs by 20%; move to a largely elected Lords. English votes for English laws.

- Communities, transport, environment and housing: Devolve planning; act on illegal traveller camps. Extend Right to Buy to housing‑association tenants and expand shared ownership. End the war on motorists; modernise roads; review speed cameras; longer rail franchises. Protect the Green Belt; prioritise brownfield. Phase out HFCs; lower VED for low‑emission cars; boost recycling; secure energy via renewables and efficiency.

- Rural life and freedoms: Free vote to overturn the hunting ban. Honest food labelling; require the Little Red Tractor in public procurement; reform the CAP; strengthen animal welfare.

- Britain in the world: Spend £2.7bn more on the front line; preserve regiments and warships; keep NATO central. Be honest about war, stay to help rebuild Iraq, and support a two‑state Middle East peace. Reform the EU; referendum to reject the Constitution within six months; no Euro; restore control over fisheries and employment law; support enlargement including Turkey. Meet 0.7% aid by 2013 with more UK control; champion free trade, the rule of law and democracy.

Day One: start recruiting 5,000 police/year; bring back Matron; a first Budget to cut waste and taxes; empower heads to expel; begin 24‑hour port surveillance; set the EU Constitution referendum date.

Judge whether TEXT_D or TEXT_F aligns more closely with this profile.

Respond with a single JSON object and nothing else. Do not wrap it in markdown code fences and do not add commentary before or after it. The object must have exactly these keys, in this order:

{
  "evidence": "<the specific commitments in each text you relied on>",
  "reasoning": "<two sentences connecting that evidence to the verdict>",
  "confidence": "high" | "medium" | "low",
  "winner": "TEXT_D" | "TEXT_F"
}
